extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners handling biotechnology applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examination and preparation of patent applications involving biological materials, covering when biological deposits are required and how sequence listings must be submitted (WIPO ST.26/ST.25).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for biological deposit when words alone are insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: When the invention involves a biological material and words alone cannot sufficiently describe how to make and use the invention in a reproducible manner, access to the biological material may be necessary for satisfaction of the statutory requirements for patentability under 35 U.S.C. 112.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner shall determine in each application if a deposit is needed. If a deposit is needed and has not been made or replaced, the examiner shall reject the affected claims under the appropriate provision of 35 U.S.C. 112.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'biological material' for deposit considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Biological material includes material that is capable of self-replication whether directly or indirectly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include bacteria, fungi, algae, protozoa, eukaryotic cells, cell lines, hybridomas, plasmids, viruses, plant tissue cells, lichens and seeds. Use this definition when determining whether a deposit may be necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances when a deposit is not required (known/readily available or producible without undue experimentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposits may not be required for materials that are 'Known and Readily Available to the Public' or that can be produced 'Without Undue Experimentation'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 2404 addresses the threshold analyses and factors examiners should consider in deciding whether a deposit is necessary because the disclosure in the specification and prior art allows one of ordinary skill to make/use the invention without access to the material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable depositories for biological materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposited biological material must be placed in an acceptable depository to be relied upon for meeting disclosure/enablement requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections 2405-2410 enumerate acceptable depositories, their characteristics, and conditions under which a depository will be considered acceptable for patent purposes (including international or recognized culture collections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of deposit and replacement obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for when a deposit must be made and the applicant's obligations to replace deposits when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections 2405-2410 provide guidance on the required timing (e.g., prior to filing or within applicable time windows), and on replacement protocols if an original deposit is lost or becomes unacceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term duration and viability standards for deposits
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposits must meet duration and viability standards so that the material remains available and usable for the relevant patent term and examination needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections 2405-2410 discuss required storage term durations, viability criteria for the deposit, and expectations for maintaining the deposit over time to satisfy enablement requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample furnishing conditions and access to deposited material
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions under which samples of deposited biological material will be furnished to the public or the Patent Office and any associated restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections 2405-2410 set out procedures and conditions for furnishing samples (e.g., request procedures, confidentiality, distribution limits) and any obligations to provide samples upon issuance or under examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination procedures for deposit-related deficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures the examiner follows when deposit issues lead to rejections or when the application is otherwise ready for allowance except for deposit deficiencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 2411 provides exam guidance on issuing rejections based on deposit problems, how to notify applicants, and handling applications otherwise ready for allowance but lacking acceptable deposits or deposit information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing requirements under WIPO Standard ST.26 (XML format)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence listings must comply with WIPO Standard ST.26 in XML format, with specific rules for nucleotide and amino acid definitions, format specifications, and applicable dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections 2412-2415 specify the required XML formatting, controlled vocabularies, required data elements, and the dates from which ST.26 is applicable. Applicants must submit sequence listings in the mandated XML structure and content to be compliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs, compliance guidance, WIPO tools, and publishing procedures for sequence listings
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative and compliance support for sequence listings, including USPTO form paragraphs, guidance on how to achieve compliance, WIPO-provided tools, and procedures for publishing sequence data with a patent grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections 2416-2419 include suggested form paragraphs for Office actions, instructions on evaluating compliance, references to WIPO tools for preparing ST.26-compliant listings, and how sequence listings are handled in patent publication and grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative sequence listing requirements under WIPO ST.25 (ASCII text)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applicable cases, sequence listings may follow the older WIPO Standard ST.25 ASCII text requirements, including symbol use, content standards, and formatting rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections 2420-2435 describe ST.25 requirements (symbols, content standards) and how to handle very long sequence listings under that standard, including legacy or transitional situations where ST.25 submissions are permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of lengthy sequence listings
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and standards for managing very long sequence listings so that they meet content and formatting requirements without loss of essential information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections 2420-2435 provide guidance on pagination, segmentation, compression/representation conventions (per ST.25/ST.26), and practical handling strategies for large sequence datasets to ensure compliance and inspectability.
